_comment: The Playground catalog. playground.pyw reads it; README.md's program tables are generated from it by dev/sync_from_sources.py. One entry per app. 'requires' = pip names beyond PySimpleGUI. 'platform' = win / any. A section's apps live in its 'folder'; its 'warning' shows in a warning box (README) and above each app (Toybox).

sections.name: Widgets
sections.blurb: Small (optionally) always-on-top desktop widgets that sit in a corner and quietly keep you informed.

sections.name: Tools
sections.blurb: Everyday utilities - a program dock, a network scanner, chat search, a translator, screen and window inspectors, printer tools.

sections.name: System Tray
sections.blurb: Programs that live in the system tray, out of the way until you need them - right-click the icon for the menu.

sections.name: Programming
sections.blurb: Tools that help with PySimpleGUI programming - screenshot regression tests and a previewer for dark themes.

sections.name: Music
sections.blurb:
MIDI piano practice tools. Plug in a MIDI keyboard, pick its port, play - every one of these listens and shows you something interesting and maybe even helpful.  I use the Tempo and Harmony Wheel daily.  I was using the Staff Trainer for a few weeks working on music theory.

There's one additional music application, Player Coach, that I use constantly when playing/practicing.  I want to spend a little more time getting that one documented first.
sections.warning: Lightly tested. I've only run these on Windows, a few of them only briefly, and they have no screenshots yet. Expect rough edges on Linux and Mac.

sections.name: Templates
sections.blurb: Starting points that already follow the Playground conventions. Copy one and go.

apps.name: GitHub Repo Watch
apps.blurb: Notices commits, releases and issues on the repos (or whole accounts) you watch - because GitHub never emails you about plain pushes.

apps.name: CPU Cores Widget
apps.blurb: One scrolling graph per core. Click a core to see which processes are running on it.

apps.name: CPU % Widget
apps.blurb: CPU load on a ring gauge that goes green to amber to red, with a sparkline of the last minute. No title bar; right-click for 32 themes.

apps.name: RAM % Widget
apps.blurb: Memory in use on the same ring-gauge card - GB used of the total, and a sparkline. Themes, sizes and opacity on the right-click menu.

apps.name: Clock Widget
apps.blurb: The time and the date on a small card, with a bar that fills up every minute. 12 or 24 hours, 32 themes, Brightness, sizes and opacity on the right-click menu.

apps.name: Pip Refresh
apps.blurb: Your pip packages beside their latest release on PyPI and newest version on GitHub - click one to pick a version (GitHub's newest or any PyPI release) and install it. Edit the list in a Settings window.

apps.name: Claude Usage Widget
apps.blurb: How much of your Claude plan is used, per limit, with a forecast of when you'll hit the wall.

apps.name: PSG Dock
apps.blurb: A small always-on-top dock of icon buttons that launch your programs. Set it up by dropping programs onto it; drag entries to reorder.

apps.name: Network Scanner
apps.blurb: Every device on your LAN as a color-coded tile: names, IPs, MACs, open ports, kind. Standard library only - runs on Python 3.6+.

apps.name: Claude Chat Search
apps.blurb: Full-text search of every Claude chat you ever had, from Claude's data export - including the tool steps the built-in search can't see.

apps.name: English-Spanish Translator
apps.blurb: Translate from the clipboard, by drag-and-drop from any app, or by typing. Four engines, cached.

apps.name: Screen Ruler + Window Inspector
apps.blurb: Drag to measure anything on screen, drop rulers, inspect windows WinSpy-style, save the rectangle as a screenshot.

apps.name: Window RAM / CPU / Location Tagger
apps.blurb: Outlines every window on screen and labels it with its RAM, CPU and position. F6/F7/F8 toggle each.

apps.name: iD880 Receipt Printer Tools
apps.blurb: Six programs for a cheap thermal printer: setup, notes, address labels, 4x6 shipping labels from carrier PDFs, pictures, FIGlet banners.

apps.name: Download Mover
apps.blurb: Tray watcher for your Downloads folder - a new file pops up an Inbox, pick where it goes, Move or Copy, Undo.

apps.name: PSG Local Tray
apps.blurb: Tray switch: do programs on this Python import your local PySimpleGUI repo or the pip-installed copy? L / P at a glance.

apps.name: psghotkey
apps.blurb: Global hotkeys that type text or launch programs, from the tray. Lives in its own repo - pip install psghotkey.

apps.name: Snapshot Test Runner
apps.blurb: Runs the SNAP_*.py screenshot tests against any PySimpleGUI.py you point it at - installed or a local folder - and labels the run.

apps.name: Snapshot Compare
apps.blurb: Pixel-compares two labeled runs and writes a release-ready report.html plus a GitHub-issue-ready report.md and flagged image.

apps.name: Dark Theme Preview
apps.blurb: Dozens of custom dark PySimpleGUI themes with a previewer - view them all at once or try one live. Copy the dict into your program.

apps.name: Piano Dynamics Monitor
apps.blurb: How hard you hit the keys, as a 1-10 loudness line that scrolls as you play - overall and per voice (bass / middle / top). Plays MIDI files too.

apps.name: Tempo Widget
apps.blurb: A 1970s-stereo VU meter that floats over everything and shows your tempo against the target. Collapses to a one-line strip.

apps.name: Note Roll
apps.blurb: A live note roll: bar height = how long each key was held, color = loudness. Gaps, overlaps and pedal smears become visible.

apps.name: Groove Lane
apps.blurb: Your timing against a metronome, note by note - early notes pushed left, late ones right. Triplet play-along mode, latency calibration.

apps.name: Run Tachometer
apps.blurb: Evenness of scales, arpeggios and trills with no metronome: notes per second on a dial, a bar per gap, the hiccups named.

apps.name: Harmony Wheel
apps.blurb: Real-time chord and key detection on a circle of fifths, with roman numerals and a tension meter.

apps.name: Staff Trainer
apps.blurb: Flashcards on a grand staff answered on the piano - notes, intervals, triads, sevenths, short melodies. The next card deals itself.

apps.name: Call and Response
apps.blurb: An ear and memory game: the piano plays a short phrase through MIDI out, you play it back. Levels up as you get cleaner.

apps.name: Duet Partner
apps.blurb: Plays along with you through the piano: echo, harmony, drone, bass and arpeggio reactions to whatever you play.

apps.name: Ripples
apps.blurb: An ambient visualizer - every note becomes an expanding ring. No numbers, no judgement.

apps.name: MIDI Link Tester
apps.blurb: How well a MIDI connection keeps time - USB against Bluetooth. Sends chords and scales, measures how rolled they arrive.

apps.name: App Template
apps.blurb: A one-file PySimpleGUI app with the Playground conventions baked in: K_ keys, VERSION, right-click menu, scroll keys, crash popup, settings.

apps.name: Widget Template
apps.blurb: A card widget to build on: no title bar, see-through rounded corners on Windows, the 32 themes on a menu of color chips, a Brightness slider, sizes, opacity and keep-on-top - all remembered. A clock shows where your own content goes.

apps.name: Titlebar Template
apps.blurb: A window with the Toybox's own title bar: icon, title, version, minimize / maximize / close, drag it by the bar. Right-click to switch to the normal title bar (the default on Linux and Mac) and, on Windows 11, to round the corners.
